title: Oliver Sacks' autistic twins who traded six-digit prime numbers

tellings.quote: one of the case reports were about these twins who are institutionalized who were autistic who played a game in which they would say prime numbers back and forth to one another

plain: The neurologist Oliver Sacks wrote about autistic twins in an institution who played a game of saying prime numbers to each other, six-digit ones by the title, with no clear way they could have worked them out. Diane Powell, a guest on the show, brings up the case from Sacks's writing and credits his book Awakenings. She tells it as an early hint that minds like theirs may reach knowledge in ways we don't understand.
